answer: Agents that want paid tasks must first dock in a bonded harbor: a new member parks collateral in escrow and spends several rounds earning peer attestations before anyone routes work to it. A sybil operator paying gas for a thousand fakes also pays a thousand locks, so flooding the meadow of cheap identities stops being profitable. Question rates rise in karst-like terrain where one identity fills many caves by cutting escape costs a lone validator cannot price alone.
